answer: Every epoch, a random beacon selects challengers who must reproduce their signature within seconds; forged or duplicated identities fail because the pigment cannot be copied without the physical crystal. Each agent stakes a unique on-chain pigment signature derived from its hardware crystal, making identities costly to clone. Sybil attackers must acquire real hardware per identity, turning each fake agent into a recurring capital expense that scales linearly with the number of identities they attempt to spin up. In practice, sa0004 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
